item.title: Newlands to provide test of more than bat and ball for Australia
item.description: The third test will be held at the scene of the Sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal.
item.dc:creator: Nick Said
item.content:encoded: Australia return to the scene of one of the darkest days in the country’s cricket history when the series-deciding third test against South Africa starts at Newlands on Tuesday. The battle may be mental as much as one of skill for several of the Australian players, not least former captain Steve Smith, who was at the centre of the Sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal in 2018. Current skipper Pat Cummins was part of that side, as were fellow seamer Josh Hazlewood and spinner Nathan Lyon, though they say they had no knowledge of the attempt to alter the condition of the ball with a piece of sandpaper. Smith bore the brunt of the considerable fallout in Australia eight years ago and having not reached the heights he might have expected on this tour, averaging a little over 20 with the bat, he would see this as the perfect time to put that right. There has so far been little chatter in South Africa about Sandpapergate but that could change at Newlands, where the first three days’ ticket sales have been strong after sparse crowds at the first two tests in Durban and Gqeberha. "He'll be fine," Australia opener Travis Head said of Smith. "I think he showed that in 2019 in England. We support him. He's been through a lot in that space and handles it well. Sometimes it brings the best out of him, as we've seen in the past." The series is level at 1-1 after big wins for both sides in the opening two games and Australia wicketkeeper Alex Carey told reporters on Sunday that it looked to be another good test-match pitch. "We are still a couple of days out but it looks another great surface," he said. "If you look back at Durban it was a five-day test match and a great contest between bat and ball. The same in Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha) and this should be no different." There has never been a test match played at Newlands in October, and just three in November, all against Australia. The tourists won the first two in 1902 and 1921, but the most recent November fixture was an eight-wicket victory for South Africa in 2011 when Australia were famously bowled out for 47 in their second innings. South Africa will be without fast bowler Anrich Nortje, who injured his groin in the second test. Captain Temba Bavuma said they would pick horses for courses in terms of his replacement. "You’ve got guys like Gerald (Coetzee), Pato (Dane Paterson), as well as (Corbin) Bosch, and we have Sen (Senuran Muthusamy) as well, so the options are there," he said. "Whoever we decide, we’ll be confident they form part of our best XI for the conditions."

item.title: Beirut's $13 chicken sandwich becomes symbol of Lebanon divide
item.description: Seven years after Lebanon’s devastating financial meltdown, a debate over a chicken sandwich has exposed an increasingly stark divide between those who can still spend freely and those struggling to get by.
item.dc:creator: Nazih Osseiran, Raghed Waked, Emilie Madi
item.content:encoded: Seven years after Lebanon’s [USN:L6N41Y0N8 TEXT:"devastating financial meltdown"], a debate over a chicken sandwich has exposed an increasingly stark divide between those who can still spend freely and those struggling to get by. A trendy health restaurant wanted to offer its calorie-conscious customers a healthier take on the beloved Levantine wrap known as the shish taouk. So, The Glow Paradise launched the “Chic Taouk”, pricing it at around $13 — nearly double what an un-chic chicken sandwich typically goes for in Beirut. The pricy pun proved hard to swallow, with outraged critics accusing the restaurant of overcharging in a country where many households struggle to afford basic necessities. Yet while the debate raged on social media, customers kept buying. The Glow Paradise sold more than 20,000 Chic Taouk sandwiches in just 11 days, according to managing partner Hrag Jeghalian, who described the online exchanges as "natural marketing". The contrasting reactions touched a nerve in Lebanon, where years of financial turmoil, political dysfunction and conflict have reshaped the country's social landscape, hollowing out much of the middle class while leaving a smaller group of consumers able to sustain an affluent lifestyle. DEBATE PULLS FOCUS AWAY FROM URGENT CRISES Sami Nader, an economist at the Saint Joseph University of Beirut, said the throngs at The Glow Paradise belied another reality. “So you see people in the restaurant, but what you don't see is that 22 restaurants closed last month,” Nader told Reuters. Lebanon’s Instagram-active community was split between those accusing the restaurant of theft and others saying the sandwich was intended for those who could afford it. Some questioned whether the dispute itself reflected misplaced priorities in a country grappling with urgent crises, from Israel’s[USN:L6N45P03S TEXT:" occupation"] of large swaths of the country’s south to the endemic electricity and water crises. Lebanon’s 2019 financial collapse was prompted by decades of corruption and profligate spending by the ruling elite, and several rounds of conflict since then have worsened the country’s economic outlook. GDP has declined by nearly 40% since 2019 and inflation is expected to rise to 17.5% due to rising global energy and shipping prices eating away at people’s purchasing power, according to the World Bank. The figure is more than quadruple the [USN:L1N43A0MP TEXT:"global headline inflation"] rate flagged by the International Monetary Fund in July. Four in five households in Lebanon struggle to afford basic necessities, the UN children’s agency said in September. 'PEOPLE CAN'T KEEP UP' The country’s middle class has “disappeared,” Nader said, dismantled by a series of crises including the collapse of the financial system in 2019, the 2020 Beirut Port explosion and two wars in under two years. Monthly bills from private generator operators, which provide electricity to many homes and businesses during outages on Lebanon's failing national grid, jumped by nearly 20% in August 2026 alone, bringing rates nearly 60% higher than they were in February of this year, according to the kilowatt-hour prices set by Lebanon’s energy ministry. For many, that means paying for 24/7 electricity now costs several hundred dollars a month, in a country where the minimum wage is set at $400. “Everything has become expensive, and people can’t keep up,” said Fouad Fakhreddine, a 53-year-old restaurant worker from nearby Hamra. “We are now getting paid, then getting in debt over that just to get by.” The years of economic instability, he said, have produced “a class that is living, and a class that is not dead and waiting to die from the unbearable situation it is in.” (This story has been refiled to change the name in the byline to Emilie Madi from Ahmad Al Kerdi.)

item.title: Trump campaigns in Michigan a day after Obama rallies Democrats
item.description: US President Donald Trump will rally Republicans in eastern Michigan on Sunday, a day after former President Barack Obama campaigned for Democrats in the state, underscoring its importance in next week's midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump will rally Republicans in eastern Michigan on Sunday, a day after former President Barack Obama campaigned for Democrats in the state, underscoring its importance in next week's midterm elections. Michigan has one of the nation's most competitive US Senate contests, an open-seat race between former US Representative Mike Rogers, a Republican, and Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed that will help decide control of the chamber. Despite repeatedly attacking El-Sayed from the Oval Office and at rallies across the country, the Republican president had not yet campaigned in Michigan this year. If he wins, El-Sayed would be the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. Trump has sought to paint El-Sayed as a Muslim extremist and repeatedly [USN:L1N4620ZA TEXT:"mocked his middle name,"] Mohamed, a common Muslim name. EL-SAYED SAYS AFFILIATION IS WITH THE US El-Sayed has dismissed the accusation and, in a recent advertisement, defended his religion, saying, "Faith is a thing there’s just too little of in Washington." Rogers has alleged without evidence that El-Sayed has [USN:L6N4661FE TEXT:"ties to the Muslim Brotherhood"], one of the Arab world's oldest and most influential Islamist groups. In an interview on NBC's "Meet the Press" on Sunday, Rogers said El-Sayed had not sufficiently responded to questions about those allegations. "He's a Democrat Socialist of America-aligned candidate who has these pretty radical support groups that don't like America," he said. El-Sayed has denied affiliation with the group, saying it is "shameful" for Rogers to question his allegiance to the United States. At Saturday's rally in Detroit, Obama framed the attacks on El-Sayed as an attempt by opponents to make him look "less patriotic and less American than they are." The former president compared it to his experience as the target of [USN:KBN23O2P2 TEXT:"false claims"] that he was born in Kenya. "We have seen this movie before," Obama said. "I starred in it ... This stuff didn't work on me. Not in Michigan. It's not going to work on Abdul." MANUFACTURING INVESTMENTS Trump's rally in Port Huron, part of an area of Michigan that he won in the 2024 presidential election with more than 66% of the vote, will also highlight the US-Canada tariff standoff. The trade fight has affected the Detroit-based [USN:L6N44N11O TEXT:"US auto industry,"] prompting Rogers to distance himself from the president's policy. Rogers on Sunday hailed Trump's tariffs for securing manufacturing investments for Michigan by Chevrolet and Detroit Diesel, but said "the automobile portion of these Canadian tariffs worries me a little bit." "There's some good and there's some things we have to work on," he told "Meet the Press." In a Fox News interview ahead of Sunday's rally, Trump praised Rogers as someone who shares Michigan voters' beliefs. "He's going to be an amazing senator," Trump told the "Sunday Briefing" program. "Solid as a rock. Apple pie." Democrats need a net gain of four seats in both the US Senate and House of Representatives to overturn Republicans' narrow 53-47 and 218-214 majorities.

item.title: How Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy sites deepened the rift with Trump
item.description: The two have long had a testy relationship, but Trump's frustration over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure triggered a crisis that Kyiv's supporters fear could threaten vital US support.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: Relations between US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy took a sharp downward turn in recent weeks, with each leader openly criticizing the other. The two have long had a testy relationship, but Trump's frustration over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure triggered a crisis that Kyiv's supporters fear could threaten vital US support going forward. Here's how the relationship soured: WHAT IS THE HISTORY OF TRUMP-ZELENSKIY TENSIONS? Trump has been skeptical of US involvement in Ukraine ever since his first term when, shortly after taking office in early 2017, he was asked to provide lethal aid to Ukraine and approved the sale of Javelin missiles to Kyiv. “Everyone around him wanted him to do it, and they pushed him hard and he eventually signed off on selling them Javelins, very reluctantly,” said a former senior Trump administration official, who spoke on condition of anonymity. “He didn’t consider it a core US interest. It was a European issue.” Trump's first major encounter with Zelenskiy came in a July 2019 phone call in which the Republican president asked the Ukrainian leader to investigate his Democratic rival Joe Biden and his son Hunter, in exchange for military support Congress had authorized. That episode led to Trump's first impeachment. Biden beat Trump in the 2020 presidential election. Trump also has fostered a relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin that runs against the norms of US foreign policy but echoes his warm ties with authoritarian leaders Xi Jinping of China and North Korea's leader Kim Jong Un. “Trump has always wanted better relations with Russia,” the former official said. WHAT DEEPENED THE RIFT BETWEEN THE TWO LEADERS? Trump's current frustration centers on Kyiv's [USN:S8N41C0VK TEXT:"attacks on Russian diesel infrastructure"]. Diesel prices have hit record highs since the US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February, and global energy costs spiked. US lawmakers in Trump's Republican party face voter anger over inflation ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. On September 13, Trump began publicly calling on Ukraine to stop targeting diesel infrastructure. The following week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was also concerned that Ukraine had hit US-linked oil shipments. Ukraine has refused to halt the strikes, saying its long-range drone campaign is its only viable response to nearly five years of Russian bombardment. Moscow was forced in July to ban diesel exports as part of a raft of measures to address domestic fuel shortages. Angered by Zelenskiy’s defiance, Trump on October 9 announced a deal to buy diesel from Moscow, issuing a temporary general license that allows Russian diesel to reach the global market. He also waived sanctions on Russia authorized by a bill he signed into law in September. Suriya Jayanti, a former US official who runs a power sector company in Ukraine, said Russia’s strikes on Ukraine’s power grid have increased, despite Trump unilaterally announcing an [USN:FWN45X008 TEXT:"energy ceasefire"] on October 11. "It is clear to everyone in Kyiv that the goal is not actually an energy ceasefire, but it is really just an effort to hobble Ukraine and give Russia a decisive advantage," said Jayanti, who is also a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council think tank. HAS THE US THREATENED TO CUT OFF SUPPORT TO UKRAINE? Zelenskiy has said Ukrainian military officials had been threatened by US counterparts, who said continuing the energy strikes would lead the US to cut off intelligence sharing. A US official familiar with the situation disputed Kyiv's account. Speaking on condition of anonymity, the US official said there has been no increase in pressure on Ukraine. “We don't have to pressure Zelenskiy. If he wants to make a deal he'll make a deal. I think Putin is putting a ton of pressure on him and he (Zelenskiy) is putting some pressure on Russia but Russia doesn't seem to be minding it as much even though they are getting hit." On Thursday, Trump said he had asked SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to restore Ukraine’s access to the company's Starlink satellite system. Starlink's disruption temporarily hampered Kyiv's military drone operations and spurred fears that Kyiv would be left defenseless against Russia's attacks going into the winter. WHAT IS THE STATUS OF MOSCOW-KYIV PEACE TALKS? Peace efforts have continued but so far have not yielded tangible results. At talks in Oslo on October 20, Ukraine presented new proposals, and Trump’s son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner repeated Trump's demand that Ukraine stop attacking Russian diesel refineries. The next day, envoy Witkoff – a close friend of Trump's - met Putin in St. Petersburg. Putin agreed to release detained American Stephen Hubbard in what the two countries called a goodwill gesture. Zelenskiy said on Friday that negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US would meet in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November, a possible precursor to a meeting of the three countries’ leaders. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February.

item.title: Jordan church attack survivor says her cousin died before her eyes
item.description: When gunmen opened fire on a church in Jordan, Sahar al-Halsa hid behind a pillar as she heard the shooting and people screaming in panic during a funeral service for her cousin's daughter.
item.dc:creator: Abdelhadi Ramahi
item.content:encoded: When gunmen opened fire on a church in Jordan, Sahar al-Halsa hid behind a pillar as she heard the shooting and people screaming in panic during a funeral service for her cousin's daughter. When she rushed outside in the chaos, she said she spotted the assailants and another cousin lying on the ground wounded. "I went to him and said: 'Assem, Assem, my darling, answer me'," she said. She said he opened his eyes to look at her, but then "he was gone". Friday's attack on the Greek Orthodox place of worship in Karak governorate, about 120 km (75 miles) southwest of the capital Amman, prompted King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against Islamist militant groups, to order security forces to respond with an "iron fist" to what authorities described as extremist terrorism. PRIEST SENDS MESSAGE OF LOVE AND PEACE Nine people died in the shooting that witnesses said lasted for several minutes. The funeral services were held on Sunday. Eight of the victims’ coffins were wrapped in Jordanian flags before they were buried in a graveyard in the village of Hamoud, where the attack took place. Mourners and priests gathered at the scene. Forty people were wounded in the rare attack on minority Christians. Speaking from her home, from where the red dome of St George's church is visible, al-Halsa concluded that God must have saved her. "My life starts now, because I was going to die," she said, speaking beside her husband Ziad al-Halsa. A statue of Jesus on a cross was displayed on a shelf. Authorities have said they are still searching for the attackers, adding it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan. There has been no immediate claim of responsibility. Ziad said he ran the short distance to the church after he heard the gunfire, describing the overwhelming sense of relief when he realised Sahar, who he described as "the love of his life", was safe. "To my cousins, may God have mercy on them," he said. Such attacks are highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable state in the Middle East, though authorities there say they have foiled several Islamist plots in recent years. Speaking ahead of the funerals, priest Yuhanna Hamati said: "Our message from this church, from this place where this horrific crime was committed, is a message of love, peace, and reassurance. A message that we send to the whole world."

item.title: Employees group warns of major Swiss job losses if UBS relocates
item.description: As many as 12,000 UBS jobs in Switzerland could be at risk if tougher capital rules prompt the bank to relocate, according to the Swiss Bank Employees Association, or SBPV.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: As many as 12,000 UBS (UBSG.S) jobs in Switzerland could be at risk if tougher capital rules prompt the bank to relocate, according to the Swiss Bank Employees Association, or SBPV. In a letter to lawmakers first published at the weekend by newspaper NZZ am Sonntag, the association warned that a relocation, sale or merger of UBS could cost 10,000 to 12,000 of UBS's roughly 34,000 jobs in Switzerland. The letter, which was also seen by Reuters, described this as the "worst case" scenario, and comes on top of cuts already made at the bank as it completes it integration of fallen rival Credit Suisse, which it acquired in 2023. UBS, which has repeatedly said it wants to remain in Switzerland, declined to comment on the SBPV estimate. A UBS spokesperson said the bank would keep job cuts resulting from the Credit Suisse takeover as low as possible. UBS said it still expects around 3,000 layoffs in Switzerland under the integration and that these would occur over several years, largely via steps like natural turnover, early retirements and insourcing of jobs once held externally. The SBPV warning comes as a committee in the lower house of the Swiss parliament [USN:L1N45N0NB TEXT:"prepares"] to discuss how much capital UBS should have to hold to back its foreign subsidiaries. Last month, the upper house [USN:L8N45F0DE TEXT:"proposed"] UBS should back those units with 90% Common Equity Tier 1 capital. UBS suggested that is [USN:L1N45C05I TEXT:"too much"] and the bank's chairman has warned it would need to carefully [USN:L8N4590WE TEXT:"consider"] its future in Switzerland if the rules are too harsh. Some shareholders of the bank have called for UBS to [USN:L1N45N061 TEXT:"leave"] Switzerland, and the bank has been [USN:L1N46205Q TEXT:"drafting"] potential contingency plans including shifting its headquarters or merging with another lender, sources have told Reuters. The SBPV letter, which also said UBS had a duty to commit to its Swiss base, urged lawmakers to pursue a "viable compromise" that did not impose such a heavy burden on the bank.

HONG KONG, Oct 25 : American John Catlin showed nerves of steel as he held local favourite Matthew Cheung and Finnish opponent Kalle Samooja at bay to win the Hong Kong Open, hitting seven birdies in Sunday's final round to finish five strokes ahead of his nearest challengers. Catlin, who won the Asian Tour Order of Merit in 2024, hit a six-under 64 in the fourth round to finish 20-under, earning his seventh title on the tour. Samooja led Cheung by a stroke going into the tricky 18th hole, but hit a bogey and had to settle for a joint second-place finish, as the latter secured the best finish for a Hong Kong player at the tournament in Fanling. "It's very, very special. Any time you can be on a trophy with some of the greatest players that ever played the game, I just feel very humble and very grateful," said Catlin.

The 35-year-old was jointly leading the scoreboard along with Thomas Pieters and Caleb Surratt after the third round, where Cheung slipped from the top with three bogeys on Saturday. A clinical Catlin shook off a bogey on the fifth hole to take a solo lead on Sunday, and quickly fixed a mistake on the 14th as he found the centre of the green with a precise 120-yard stroke from thick grass to stay on course for a birdie. Error-prone Pieters and Surratt finished tied for sixth place with Sampson Zheng. Catlin's first trophy on the Asian Tour since April 2024 also earned him an invitation to next year's Open Championship and a maiden qualification for the Masters. "It's like a dream come true... it's been a long time coming, lot of hard work, lot of times when you weren't sure what was coming but you just kind of held the faith and I just kept working," Catlin said, shaking his head. "To finally be at the Masters, speechless."

item.title: Russia says it hit two cargo vessels and Ukrainian logistics hubs
item.description: The Russian Defence Ministry said on Sunday that its drones had struck a cargo vessel bound for the Black Sea port of Chornomorsk in an overnight attack and another cargo vessel en route to the port of Odesa during the day.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Russian Defence Ministry said on Sunday that its drones had struck a cargo vessel bound for the Black Sea port of Chornomorsk in an overnight attack and another cargo vessel en route to the port of Odesa during the day. The ministry said the vessels were being used to supply the Ukrainian army. Russian forces also hit a logistics centre, a distribution centre and a logistics terminal in the Ukrainian city of Kharkiv overnight. The ministry said the facilities had been used for storage and distribution of dual-use cargo for the Ukrainian military. Reuters could not independently verify the Defence Ministry's information.

item.title: Four killed in two drone attacks in Russia's Belgorod region
item.description: A Ukrainian drone attack overnight on the Russian border city of Belgorod killed three people and injured 13, local authorities said on Sunday, while a separate drone strike later in the day killed another person and wounded one other in a nearby village.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Ukrainian drone attack overnight on the Russian border city of Belgorod killed three people and injured 13, local authorities said on Sunday, while a separate drone strike later in the day killed another person and wounded one other in a nearby village. "Unfortunately, the death toll from last night's attack (in the city of Belgorod) has risen — another man who had been injured has died in hospital. This is a great tragedy for all the city's residents," Belgorod's mayor, Valentin Demidov, wrote on state-backed messaging app MAX. The overnight attack on Belgorod damaged 30 apartment buildings, 35 cars, four houses, three administrative buildings, eight commercial premises and three social facilities, regional governor Alexander Shuvayev said. In a separate incident on Sunday morning, one person was killed and another injured when a Ukrainian drone struck a car in the village of Voznesenovka near the town of Shebekino, local authorities said.

item.title: バルセロナで「反体制」暴徒が略奪・放火、ブリュッセルでは警察と衝突
item.description: [バルセロナ／ブリュッセル ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[バルセロナ／ブリュッセル ２４日 ロイター] - スペインのバルセロナで２４日夜、反体制を掲げた抗議活動の一部参加者が市中心部で店舗を略奪、路上の公共設備に放火するなど暴徒化し、約１００人が拘束された。抗議活動はソーシャルメディア（ＳＮＳ）で呼びかけられ、多くの若者が参加していた。ベルギーの首都ブリュッセルでも同日、反政府デモ隊と警察が衝突するなど、各地で混乱が続いている。

現場となったバルセロナのカタルーニャ広場は観光客や地元の買い物客でにぎわう市内有数の人気スポットで、カタルーニャ自治州の当局によると周辺の１４店舗が被害を受け、放火も３０件以上あった。拘束された人の約４分の１は未成年だという。ＳＮＳに投稿された動画には、フードを被った黒ずくめの一群が店の窓ガラスを蹴破り商品を奪って逃走する様子が映っており、一部ではオンラインの視聴者が破壊・略奪行為をあおる場面もみられた。

今回のデモは、ＳＮＳ上で「体制に反対する」運動への参加を呼びかける形で広まった。フランスで抗議活動を展開してきた学生たちを動員するために使われた「憤慨する高校生たち」というキャッチフレーズも掲げられていた。

若者を中心に数百人が抗議活動に参加したブリュッセルでは、警察に追われて転倒したデモ参加者を警察官が暴行する場面や、デモ隊が自転車や道路標識などを積み上げて火を放とうとする場面をロイター記者が目撃。別の場所では、警察が催涙ガスを使ったとの現地報道もあった。ただ、前の週に起きた衝突ほど大規模化せず、地元警察は大きな事件は発生しなかったと発表した。

item.title: Most Gulf shares close lower as Saudi-Houthi fighting rages on
item.description: Most Gulf bourses ended lower on Sunday and Saudi Arabia's index registered its worst session in 18 months as fighting between the kingdom and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis showed no sign of abating.
item.dc:creator: Ateeq Shariff
item.content:encoded: Most Gulf bourses ended lower on Sunday and Saudi Arabia's index registered its worst session in 18 months as fighting between the kingdom and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis showed no sign of abating. Saudi air defences downed drones and missiles over Riyadh and the south on Sunday, [USN:L2N46A05D TEXT:"the Saudi-led coalition said"]. A day earlier, the Houthis said they [USN:L2N46A00K TEXT:"hit Saudi oil facilities and airports"] and the Saudi-led coalition said it downed two missiles. Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI) pared losses to finish 2.7% lower after falling as much as 3.4%. The index posted its worst intraday performance since April 2025, with heavyweight Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) falling 0.9%. GCC stocks stayed under pressure as tensions and shipping disruptions in key waterways kept investors wary. Fears of renewed US military action dented de-escalation hopes, with traders awaiting diplomatic progress, said George Pavel, general manager at Naga.com Middle East. In Qatar, the index (.QSI) reversed early losses to inch 0.1% higher. Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index (.EGX30) plunged 3.6%, its biggest single-day fall since June 2025, with most of its constituents in negative territory. Saudi Arabia (.TASI) declined 2.7% to 9,439 Qatar (.QSI) inched 0.1% higher to 8,615 Egypt (.EGX30) dropped 3.6% to 49,234 Bahrain (.BAX) eased 0.2% to 1,849 Oman (.MSX30) retreated 1.4% to 7,278 Kuwait (.BKP) added 0.5% to 8,768

item.title: Brazil votes in tight runoff between Lula and Bolsonaro
item.description: Corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling dominated the race.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes, Marta Nogueira
item.content:encoded: Brazilians voted on Sunday in a tight runoff vote that could move Latin America's largest nation sharply rightward, bringing it closer to the United States as part of a broader conservative shift across the region. The runoff pits leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former President Jair Bolsonaro. Flavio scored [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"a major upset at the start of the month"] by defying pollsters to lead voting in the first round. A victory for Bolsonaro, 45, would extend a wave of right-wing victories for Latin American candidates friendly to US President Donald Trump, while a fourth mandate for Lula would be a disappointment in Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security. WASHINGTON DENIES ACCUSATIONS OF MEDDLING Reuters on Saturday [USN:L1N4650X8 TEXT:"revealed a campaign"] within Trump's State Department to help get the Bolsonaros back in power. Trump has so far declined to endorse a candidate. Asked on Sunday who he hoped would win, Trump declined to say. "I don’t want to get into that, but we are watching," he told reporters in Washington. Brazil's election race has been dominated by corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling, which Washington denies. It has also been colored by fallout from [USN:L1N43T0Q4 TEXT:"Jair Bolsonaro's 2025"] conviction for plotting a 2022 coup, with Flavio pledging to free his father if elected. Trump has called the case a "witch hunt" and imposed a 50% tariff on Brazil in 2025, in a decision explicitly linked to Jair Bolsonaro’s trial. While this was later watered down, Trump unleashed [USN:L1N43P1HE TEXT:"new levies against Brazil this year"], citing unfair trade practices. Lula has cast the Trump administration’s proximity to the Bolsonaro clan as part of an attempt to sway the election, while labeling tariffs and other punitive measures as bullying. “We can’t just hand Brazil over,” said Elenildes dos Reis, a 60-year-old lawyer in Sao Paulo who voted for Lula and said his victory would be a way of standing up to Trump and what she described as a rising wave of fascism. “It won’t just be our victory, it will be the world’s,” she said. On economic issues, despite falling inequality and unemployment, Lula has struggled to win over an electorate grappling with high living costs and heavy household debt. Endemic gang violence also weighs on voters’ minds. Bolsonaro has sought to capitalize on cost-of-living concerns and has promised a heavy-handed approach to fighting crime, pledging maximum-security jails and chemical castration for serious sexual offenses. “We need change,” said Jose Carlos Jarra, a 61-year-old retiree in Sao Paulo who worked in healthcare and voted for Bolsonaro. He hoped the senator would tackle public security and do more for retirees, calling Brazil’s minimum wage “a disgrace.” In Rio de Janeiro, 75-year-old retiree Alba Marques said her vote for Bolsonaro was a vote against Lula's Workers' Party, not for Bolsonaro. "I can’t stand 40 years of a guy saying he’s going to fix Brazil anymore. The same promise," she said. CANDIDATES ARE NECK AND NECK Casting his ballot in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday, Bolsonaro urged people to come out to vote "come rain or shine." Lula voted in Sao Bernardo do Campo, near Sao Paulo, and thanked his supporters. "What the people did for me these past few days is something I can never repay," he told reporters. Polls show the candidates practically tied going into the runoff. Historical precedent favors Bolsonaro, however, as no candidate has ever won the presidency after coming second in the first-round vote. Bolsonaro picked up 47% of ballots cast in the first round, while Lula trailed with 45%. The senator's first-round win [USN:L6N45Q08A TEXT:"sent Brazil's markets and currency soaring"] on expectations of pro-business reforms. His first-round success was mirrored in congressional elections for his Liberal Party and other right-wing politicians, which could pave a legislative path for him, or complicate governance for Lula.

item.title: Disenchanted Netanyahu supporters are prize of Israel election campaign
item.description: Labor has dwindled to a rump as Israeli politics have shifted rightwards, and there are now around half a dozen other parties courting Likud voters, from the center to the far right.
item.dc:creator: Emily Rose, Maayan Lubell
item.content:encoded: In the remote Negev Desert town of Dimona, long a bastion of Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party, disenchanted voters are going door-to-door campaigning for his top rival, hoping to bring down the veteran prime minister in Israel's election on Tuesday. The ballot is Israel's first since Hamas' October 7, 2023, surprise attack that shook the country and plunged the region into turmoil, as Israel went to war on the militant group in Gaza and its allies in Lebanon and Iran. The October 7 security breach saw Likud's popularity plummet. Opinion polls for months have predicted Netanyahu's coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties losing its majority. But his top rival, centrist Gadi Eisenkot, has no clear path to power either, and the race has become tighter as the election nears. Dimona, where an Iranian missile wounded dozens in March, has become a political battleground. "We must have change. Bibi has to go," said Yossi Assayag, 74, who says he has supported Likud most his life. "Bibi has brought disaster to Israel." LIKUD LOYALISTS Assayag is part of a cohort of town residents trying to convince their community to vote for Eisenkot's party Yashar, which is neck-and-neck with Likud in the polls. It's a tough task in Dimona, where half the voters in the previous 2022 election cast a ballot for Likud. "I will never betray Likud," said Ruti Ohana, a pensioner, who says she has voted Likud ever since immigrating to Israel from North Africa more than 60 years ago. She said Netanyahu was a cut above his rivals, and the blame he receives from detractors for October 7 was unfair. Right-wing Likud long ago formed a core voter base among Jews of Middle Eastern and North African descent, known as Mizrahis, who felt neglected by the European-influenced centre-left Labor Party that dominated Israel for generations. Labor has since dwindled to a rump as Israeli politics have shifted rightwards, and there are now around half a dozen other parties courting Likud voters, from the centre to the far right. But the link to the party among its past supporters remains strong. "Most people here vote for Likud just because that's how they were raised," said Oria Asaf, 25, a past Likud voter now backing Yashar. "The change will come when people start to think about their children's future rather than their parents' past." BATTLE FOR WAVERING LIKUDNIKS While Netanyahu has a hard core of supporters that can't be won over, the prize is undecided voters who "understand that we are in a state of crisis" and are open to persuasion, said Michal Elmalem Abu, elected as a member of the city council from Likud and now leading Eisenkot's Dimona campaign. Some 13% of Israeli voters have yet to decide how they will vote, according to data collected by the Viterbi Family Center for Public Opinion and Policy Research at the Israel Democracy Institute. Of those who voted for Likud in 2022, just 55% now say they will vote for the party again on Tuesday. Fifteen percent will support parties aligned against Netanyahu, including 8% for Yashar. Another 14% will vote for alternative right-wing parties, and 9% are undecided. It is in places just like Dimona where Eisenkot stands a chance to bite a chunk out of Likud's base, said Amotz Asa-El, a political scientist at the Hartman Institute. A child of Moroccan immigrants who rose through the ranks to become military chief of staff, Eisenkot, 66, has a personal story of humble origins from the Mizrahi community that "appeals to a big swath of the Israeli electorate, particularly Likud's traditional electorate", said Asa-El. In an electoral field crowded with ex-soldiers, his peerless security credentials are an asset. The loss of his son, killed in combat in Gaza in December 2023, resonates with voters. At a town hall during a visit to Dimona in July, residents said they were excited about the prospect of a leader of Mizrahi descent. Others approached him with hugs and tearful condolences for the loss of his son. But a week later Netanyahu held his own event, demonstrating his powerful appeal in the hardscrabble Negev, where Likud governments have long boasted of bringing development funds. "Look around you, look at your community, look at what was here then and what is here now, and ask yourselves which governments invested in this monumental effort. And I do this out of immense love," he said. Lior Katzav, a Likud former mayor of Kiryat Malachi, another small-town stronghold, said party surveys show voters who had abandoned Likud are returning as the election nears. But even some who are sympathetic to Netanyahu say it may be time for a change. Israel's youngest prime minister when he was first elected 30 years ago, he has since become its longest-serving, now 77, having governed for 18 years over six terms. "It's time for him to go," said Dimona software engineer David Iskali. "He's done a lot for Israel but it can't go on. I won't give my vote to someone almost 80-years-old."

FAST

MUMBAI, Oct 25 : Mumbai's cricket fans packed the stands at the Andheri Sports Complex on Saturday to watch Indian World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav swing a bat - just not the kind that they are used to. Indian cricketers Suryakumar Yadav, Shardul Thakur, Deepak Chahar and Radha Yadav lined up alongside ex-Major League Baseball players Nick Swisher, Adrian Gonzalez, Jake Arrieta and Jonny Gomes in a three-on-three tournament that organisers pitched as a bridge between the two bat-and-ball games. Each of the four teams mixed a baseball veteran, an Indian cricketer and an American softball player and the scoring rewarded both muscle and precision. A home run earned two points, hitting the target zone earned four and fielders picked up one point for a catch, while five consecutive out-of-the-park hits doubled a team's total.

The semifinals offered up both a thriller and a stroll, as Gonzalez's Los Angeles Dodgers overturned the Shardul-led Chicago Cubs' 44 runs with just a minute to spare, while Suryakumar's New York Yankees cruised past the Boston Red Sox. That set up a rematch of the 2024 World Series, this time in India, with the Yankees posting 78 and holding off the Dodgers to be crowned champions. Softball player Rachel Garcia was named the tournament's most valuable player. Suryakumar, a former India captain who guided the side to victory at this year's Twenty20 Cricket World Cup on home soil, said he is confident baseball will grow in India and that cricketing skills can translate to success in the American sport. "I think it's all about good range hitting," added Suryakumar, whose celebrations spilled into the stands as he placed the gold chain he won around his wife's neck after the win. "You must be strong from head to your lower body, have a good core and strong arms. If you want to hit 450 feet, 500 feet, you got to be strong. Work hard. No substitutes."

item.title: Borr Drilling rig sinks off Gabon, one person dead and four missing
item.description: Borr Drilling's Prospector 5 rig sank late on Saturday off the coast of Mayumba, Gabon, killing one employee and leaving four others missing among the 115 people on board, three sources familiar with the matter said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Gnaneshwar Rajan, Colleen Goko
item.content:encoded: Borr Drilling's (BORR.N) Prospector 5 rig sank late on Saturday off the coast of Mayumba, Gabon, killing one employee and leaving four others missing among the 115 people on board, three sources familiar with the matter said on Sunday. An Indian national, one of the five initially unaccounted for, has been found dead. The remaining four missing include three Gabonese nationals and one other expatriate, the sources said. The government has not confirmed the death, instead saying that five people remain missing and that search efforts were ongoing. "Preliminary information indicates that the rig experienced a punch-through event during preload activities, resulting in loss of stability and the subsequent sinking of the rig," the offshore drilling contractor said. The Prospector 5 oil and gas rig, owned and operated by Borr, is contracted to support BW Energy's (BWE.OL) drilling operations off Gabon. The rig had not yet begun drilling. Prospector 5 is located at the Dussafu Marin permit, a licence off the Gabon coast. BW Energy holds a 73.5% working interest in the licence, with Panoro Energy holding 17.5%. Gabon's Ministry of Petroleum and Gas said it had activated a crisis unit and ordered the navy to reinforce search and rescue operations at sea. The ministry also ordered a technical investigation, Petroleum and Gas Minister Clotaire Kondja said in a statement. The crisis unit brings together the ministry, the navy, state oil company Gabon Oil, BW Energy and Borr Drilling, Kondja said. The accident occurred at approximately 9:40 p.m. (2040 GMT) on Saturday in the Dussafu Marin permit area near the Mabomont production facility, the ministry said. "We are deeply concerned for those who remain unaccounted for and everyone affected by this incident," said Borr Drilling Chief Executive Bruno Morand. "Our immediate priority is supporting the ongoing search and rescue efforts and the welfare of all personnel involved." Panoro Energy (PENR.OL) said production had been halted, adding that there were no reports of damage or accidental discharges. No discharge of harmful substances has been observed, the ministry said, adding that pollution-response resources remained deployed to protect the coastline and nearby Mayumba National Park.

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝ブルワーズがＷＳで開幕2連勝、4点差からの逆転勝ち
item.description: ［ミルウォーキー ２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ミルウォーキー　２４日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は２４日、ワールドシリーズ（ＷＳ、７回戦制）の第２戦を行い、ブルワーズが地元ウィスコンシン州ミルウォーキーでレイズに５─４で逆転勝ち。対戦成績を２勝０敗とした。

ブルワーズは一回表に４点を失ったが、その裏に４番ウィリアム・コントレラス捕手と６番ギャレット・ミッチェル中堅手の適時打で２点を返した。さらに、四回に相手のエラーで１点差に迫ると、六回に８番サル・フレリック右翼手が同点ソロ。続く七回に７番クーパー・プラット遊撃手のタイムリーで逆転した。

ブルワーズは小刻みな投手リレーで二回以降、無失点。５番手で登板し、１回１／３を無安打無失点に抑えたアブナー・ウリーベ投手が勝利投手となった。

第３戦は２６日、レイズの地元フロリダ州セントピーターズバーグで行われる。これまでにＷＳで０勝２敗から逆転優勝を果たしたのは１０チームのみで、１９９６年のヤンキースが最後。

item.title: サッカー＝ドルトムントが暫定首位に浮上、バイアーが決勝ゴール
item.description: ［ドルトムント（ドイツ） ２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ドルトムント（ドイツ）　２４日　ロイター］ - サッカーのドイツ１部ブンデスリーガは２４日、各地で試合を行い、ドルトムントがアイントラハト・フランクフルトを１─０で下し、暫定ながら首位に浮上した。

なかなか得点が奪えず苦戦していたドルトムントだが、後半３５分にマクシミリアン・バイアーがペナルティーエリア手前から右足でネットを揺らし、これが決勝弾となった。フランクフルトの堂安律は先発し、後半４２分までプレー。同僚の小杉啓太はベンチ入りするも最後まで出場はなかった。

７試合を終えて無敗のドルトムントは勝ち点を１７に伸ばし、翌日に試合を控えるバイエルン・ミュンヘンに同３差をつけた。

佐野海舟が先発したマインツはブレーメンに２─３で黒星。佐野は後半アディショナルタイム１分までプレーした。チームメートの川崎颯太はベンチ外だった。田中聡がフル出場したシャルケはケルンとスコアドローで試合を終えた。

item.title: ＮＢＡ＝セブンティシクサーズ開幕3連勝、レブロンは欠場
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］　 -

米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）は２４日、各地で試合を行い、セブンティシクサーズはバックスを１２７─１１６で下し、開幕から３連勝とした。

シクサーズのジョエル・エンビードが２８得点、１１リバウンド、１０アシストでキャリア通算１０回目のトリプルダブルを記録。ジェイレン・ブラウンが２７得点、タイリース・マクシーが２６得点で貢献した。シクサーズのレブロン・ジェームズは腰の痛みを考慮して、出場メンバーを外れた。

キャバリアーズはネッツを１２５─１２１で下し、スパーズはマーベリックスに１２２─１０６で快勝。いずれも今季初勝利を挙げた。ウィザーズはトレイ・ヤングが２５得点、４リバウンド、９アシストと活躍し、ブルズを１２４─１２０で退けた。

ロケッツはホークスを１２１─１１４で下し、３勝０敗に。ヒートはホーネッツに１１０─１１５で敗れ、開幕から３試合を終えて未勝利となった。

item.title: オバマ氏、中間選挙で「愚行に歯止め」と訴え トランプ政権を痛烈批判
item.description:
Dan Catchpole
[２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Dan Catchpole

[２４日 ロイター] - 米中間選挙が来週に迫り各地で応援合戦が熱を帯びる中、接戦の中西部２州で行われた民主党の集会にオバマ元大統領が登壇した。トランプ大統領本人や政権の対イラン政策などを痛烈に批判し、中間選挙での投票は現政権の「愚行を少しでも食い止める」ための「サーキットブレーカー」であり、ブレーカーを切り替えて政府に説明責任を求めるべきだと訴えた。

ミシガン州デトロイトで上院議員候補エルサイード氏の応援に立ったオバマ氏は、トランプ氏は国民の税金で私腹を肥やし利権を売り買いする前代未聞の大統領だとし、「今や共和党は腐敗した政府、無能な政府、機能しない政府の代名詞になってしまった」と批判した。米政権が「勝利」したとしている対イラン政策では、イランがホルムズ海峡を通過する船舶の攻撃を示唆することで石油輸出国を動揺させており、結果としてイランの影響力を高めることになったと指摘した。

さらに、政権の中枢部はさまつな事柄にしか興味がなく、ヘグセス国防長官を例に挙げ「兵士の顎のラインや男性ホルモンといった『重要問題』ばかり気にしている」と皮肉り、ホワイトハウスの改装についても悪趣味だとやゆした。

ホワイトハウスはコメントの求めに即座に応じなかった。ロイターとイプソスが８月に実施した世論調査では、トランプ一族が暗号資産関連で得た収益について６３％が不適切だと回答、「大統領の政策判断は私的なビジネス上の利害関係に影響されている」との回答は６９％に上っていた。

激戦州の一つとされるミシガン州では、ピーターズ民主党上院議員の引退に伴いエルサイード候補が共和党のロジャース元下院議員と接戦を繰り広げている。オバマ氏は民主党内で依然、最も人気の高い人物の１人で、デトロイトでの集会に先立ってオハイオ州クリーブランドでも、議席奪還を目指すブラウン元上院議員の応援演説を行なった。

item.description: Oct 25 : The final Australian MotoGP at the Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit was called off on Sunday due to heavy rain, ruining the farewell for one of the championship's most beloved circuits.It was a crushing blow for the sold-out crowd at Phillip Island, with the Australian Grand Prix moving to the stree

FAST

Oct 25 : The final Australian MotoGP at the Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit was called off on Sunday due to heavy rain, ruining the farewell for one of the championship's most beloved circuits. It was a crushing blow for the sold-out crowd at Phillip Island, with the Australian Grand Prix moving to the streets of Adelaide next year. The Moto2 and Moto3 races were cancelled first and the MotoGP race was delayed by two hours due to the weather, before organisers threw in the towel and finally called it off at 3:40 p.m. (0440 GMT). "Due to limited visibility affecting the operation of the medical helicopter the MotoGP Grand Prix race has been cancelled," MotoGP said in a statement.

"The MotoGP riders will do a lap behind the safety car and stop on the main straight to greet the fans. Pitlane will open for the farewell lap at 15:45 local time." RIDER PARADE The dark clouds and pelting rain brought down the visibility around the circuit, affecting the medical helicopter, which would take 45 minutes to reach the circuit from mainland Melbourne in an emergency. Other than two years lost to the COVID-19 pandemic, the seaside track south of Melbourne had been a fixture on the world championship calendar for 30 years and produced some of Australian motorcycling's most memorable moments. Australian two-times world champion Casey Stoner celebrated six wins in succession from 2007 to 2012, while compatriot Mick Doohan sealed his fifth and final world title with victory in the 1998 race. The raincoat-clad fans who persevered through the rain were treated to a farewell lap from the MotoGP riders, who waved as they slowly made their way around a soaking wet track. Home racer Jack Miller did his best to entertain his supporters with a series of tricks, including a stand-up wheelie over the finish line, before heading over to the grandstand and throwing his gloves and boots into the crowd. MILLER DEJECTED, SIGH OF RELIEF FOR MARTIN The Pramac Racing rider, a very strong performer in the wet, cut a dejected figure when he was interviewed after completing his lap. "This is a tough pill to swallow," said the 31-year-old, who will be leaving MotoGP at the end of the season after more than a decade to join Pata Maxus Yamaha in the World Superbike Championship. "You know, I was praying for rain all weekend. We got the rain, but obviously we weren't organised enough to get the racing going, so it's a tough one. "You guys deserve better. Honestly, all of you have done a fantastic job turning out for Phillip Island, sitting through traffic, sitting through dog-shit weather, all the rest of it. You guys are amazing. Thank you very much." Rain had been expected for the weekend, but MotoGP did not revive its 2023 strategy for the circuit, when the Grand Prix was moved ahead to Saturday and the sprint scheduled for Sunday. That sprint race three years ago was eventually called off. The cancellation of the race also ended the opportunity for seven-times MotoGP champion Marquez to extend his lead in the championship standings, with his title rival Martin declared unfit to compete in the race after fracturing his wrist. Martin held the championship lead heading into the weekend but finds himself 10 points behind Marquez after failing to finish Saturday's sprint after a gruesome crash. On Sunday, Martin's team Aprilia said he would not travel back to Spain to undergo treatment, however, boosting the 2024 champion's hopes of racing at next week's Malaysian Grand Prix and remaining in the title fight.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Portuguese police clear Lisbon housing protest camp, arresting 25
item.description: Portuguese police cleared a camp in central Lisbon held to protest against the country's deepening housing crisis, baton-charging demonstrators in the early hours of Sunday and making 25 arrests.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves, Miguel Pereira
item.content:encoded: Portuguese police cleared a camp in central Lisbon held to protest against the country's deepening housing crisis, baton-charging demonstrators in the early hours of Sunday and making 25 arrests. Portugal is grappling with one of Europe's most acute home affordability crises, as prices have more than doubled since 2017 while rents for new leases have nearly doubled, with young people among the hardest hit. The Portuguese protests echo recent demonstrations in [USN:L1N45U0F8 TEXT:"Spain"] over home shortages and surging rents. There have also been protests in cities including [USN:L2N46A01A TEXT:"Paris"], where small student demonstrations over school conditions broadened into wider protests against the government's economic policies. In Portugal, dozens of officers, some with police dogs, moved in on the camp in Rossio Square shortly after 2 a.m. (0200 GMT), having warned protesters their tents would be dismantled if they weren't removed and threatening disobedience charges for those who resisted. POLICE SAY OPERATIONS 'PROPORTIONATE' Protesters had pitched more than 100 tents after Saturday's protest march by thousands along one of Lisbon's main avenues. "We have an obligation to fight for what we believe in," said one marcher, Vitor Gomes, 21, a multimedia communications student, adding that housing speculation, wealth concentration and rising inequality made him pessimistic about the future. Police said the operation was "proportionate" and that 25 people arrested for disobedience were later released and are due in court on Monday. POLICE SAY OFFICERS AND PROTESTERS INJURED A smaller camp of about 50 tents was also dismantled in Porto's Praca D. Joao I, where police made six arrests. While police reported seven minor injuries among officers and protesters in the two operations, activist group Casa para Viver (Homes to Live) said 60 people were hurt and called for a fresh protest outside parliament on Tuesday. "Choosing the early hours of the morning to unleash dogs and baton-charge peaceful protesters is a political decision. It shows this government would rather repress those denouncing the housing crisis than address it," the group said. Protesters say soaring rents and higher living costs are squeezing households and turning housing into a growing source of discontent, with young people among those hardest hit. The Bank of Portugal estimates a shortfall of 300,000 homes nationwide, equivalent to Lisbon's entire housing stock. The protesters are demanding that the government scrap a [USN:L6N45M1AX TEXT:"bill"] to make evictions easier and end rent caps on new leases, which passed a first parliamentary reading, although the far-right Chega party abstained.

item.title: Ｆ１＝米国ＧＰ予選、総合優勝目前のアントネッリがＰＰ獲得
item.description: ［オースティン（米テキサス州） ２４日 ロイター］
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［オースティン（米テキサス州）　２４日　ロイター］ -

自動車レースＦ１の今季第１８戦、米国グランプリ（ＧＰ）は２４日、米テキサス州オースティンで予選を行い、総合首位のキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア、メルセデス）がポールポジション（ＰＰ）を獲得した。

２番手にはマックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ）、３番手にはアイザック・ハジャー（フランス）とレッドブル勢が入り、シャルル・ルクレール（モナコ）が４番手、通算７回の総合優勝を誇るルイス・ハミルトン（英国）が５番手とフェラーリ勢が続いた。

同僚アントネッリとは１０２ポイント差の２位につけるジョージ・ラッセル（英国）は６番手だった。

２０歳のアントネッリは２５日の決勝で優勝し、ラッセルが９位以下、さらにハミルトンが５位以下に終わった場合、Ｆ１史上最年少王者となる。

item.title: サッカー＝バレンシア逆転負け、佐藤はベンチ入りも出番なし
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - サッカーのスペイン１部は２４日、各地で試合を行い、佐藤龍之介が所属するバレンシアはビリャレアルに１─２と逆転負けを喫し、今季２勝目を逃した。

バレンシアは前半３８分にＰＫで先制。しかし追加点が奪えないまま、後半２４分に追い付かれると、同アディショナルタイム６分に逆転ゴールを許した。佐藤はベンチ入りしたものの、最後まで出番はなかった。

アトレチコ・マドリードはフリアン・アルバレスがゴールを挙げ、デポルティボを１─０で下した。エスパニョールはラシンに１─２で敗れ、エルチェはラヨ・バリェカノに３─０で白星を飾った。

１０試合を終えてアトレチコが勝ち点を２５とし、９試合消化の首位バルセロナに同２差とした。バレンシアは開幕からわずか１勝で同６の１９位と苦しんでいる。

item.title: ラグビー＝日本協会百周年記念試合、日本は男女ともに敗戦
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - 日本ラグビー協会創立１００周年記念試合のリポビタンＤチャレンジカップが２４日、東京・秩父宮ラグビー場で行われ、世界ランキング９位の日本代表は同１０位のフィジー代表に２８─３４で競り負けた。

日本は斎藤直人、ワーナー・ディアンズ、マキシファウルアがトライを奪い、前半を２１─２１で折り返した。後半に勝ち越しトライを決められた後、ディアンズの２トライ目などで追い付いたものの、２本のＰＧで突き放された。

日本は９月に行われたパシフィック・ネーションズカップ決勝では、フィジーを２０─１５で下していた。日本は１１月、国際大会のネーションズ選手権のため英国に遠征し、７日にウェールズ代表、１４日にイングランド代表、２１日にスコットランド代表と対戦する予定。

この日は男女ダブルヘッダーとして行われ、世界ランキング１２位の女子日本代表は同１１位のウェールズ代表に０─１７で敗れた。

item.title: サッカー＝アストンビラがマンＣ撃破、ＧＫ鈴木が好セーブ連発
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグは２４日、各地で試合を行い、ＧＫ鈴木彩艶がフル出場したアストンビラが、開幕から７戦無敗だったマンチェスター・シティー（マンＣ）を２─１で下した。

アストンビラは前半６分に相手守備陣のミスを突いてニコラス・ジャクソンが先制弾。後半７分にアーリング・ハーランドのゴールで同点とされたが、その８分後に再びジャクソンが決めて勝ち越した。鈴木は前後半にわたって好セーブを連発。アストンビラはホームのマンＣ戦で４連勝とした。

坂元達裕が先発したコベントリーはフラムに０─１で黒星。坂元は後半４１分までプレーした。

その他、アーセナルはエバートンを２─０で下し、チェルシーはトットナムに０─２で敗れた。

８試合を終えてマンＣとアーセナルが勝ち点２１で並び、得失点差でマンＣが首位。アストンビラは同１１で暫定６位に浮上した。２勝６敗のコベントリーは同６で１９位に後退した。

item.title: ゴルフ＝バミューダ選手権、前日首位の平田は34位に後退
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - 米男子ゴルフのバミューダ選手権は２４日、英領バミューダ、サウサンプトンのポートロイヤルＧＣ（パー７１）で第３ラウンドを行い、前日首位の平田憲聖は通算８アンダーの３４位に後退した。

平田は２バーディー、１ダブルボギー、５ボギーの５オーバー７６とスコアを崩し、大きく順位を落とした。１３位で出た米沢蓮も２オーバー７３と伸ばせず、通算７アンダーの４４位に後退。２アンダー６９で回った金谷拓実らと並んだ。

オースティン・スマザーマン（米国）とシェイマス・パワー（アイルランド）が通算１６アンダーの首位で並んでいる。

item.title: トランプ氏、独ＶＷの工場新設を発表 接戦ジョージア州で支持獲得狙う
item.description:
Bo Erickson David Shepardson
[ペリー（米ジョージア州） ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Bo Erickson　David Shepardson

[ペリー（米ジョージア州） ２４日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２４日、独フォルクスワーゲン傘下のアウディがジョージア州に、約４０億ドルを投じてスポーツタイプ多目的車（ＳＵＶ）を年間２０万台生産する組み立て工場を建設する計画と正式に発表した。中間選挙に向け、有権者に共和党への支持を訴える狙いがある。

同州中部のメイコン近郊ペリーで開催した政治集会で明らかにした。アウディによると、来年着工し２０３０年代初頭に生産を開始予定で、約４５００人の雇用が創出される見込み。同席したデルナー最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は「米国市場を信じているからこその長期投資だ」と述べた。

ジョージア州では１１月３日の中間選挙に向け連邦上院選と州知事選が大接戦となっており、トランプ大統領は昨年導入した自動車関税が米経済にプラスになっていると訴え支持を得たい考え。共和党の議員からは「関税がなく、常識に即した規制がなく、カリフォルニア州が燃費基準を規制する権限を撤廃していなければ、（今回の工場建設は）決して実現しなかっただろう」（バーニー・モレノ上院議員、オハイオ州選出）などと賛同する声が聞かれた。

一方で、関税が自動車価格を押し上げ、通商政策の不確実性によって自動車メーカーの一部の投資が遅れたとの批判も出ている。

米国市場向けの全車両を欧州またはメキシコから輸入しているアウディは、昨年の自動車関税導入で１２億ユーロ（薬１４億ドル）の打撃を受けた。中国での競争激化も加わり販売台数は２年連続で減少、米国販売も今年これまでに１６％減少している。

item.title: フーシ派のサウジ攻撃続く、一部再開のリヤド空港も標的と警告
item.description: [２５日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[２５日 ロイター] - イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は２４日、サウジアラビアの石油施設や空港を再び攻撃したと発表した。フーシ派の攻撃を受けて閉鎖していたキング・ハリド国際空港の一部発着再開に対しても、引き続き同空港を「軍事目標」と見なしており利用を控えるよう改めて警告した。

フーシ派の軍事報道官は、攻撃では西部ヤンブーにある国営石油会社サウジアラムコの施設やラービグの石油精製所、原油ポンプ施設、東西パイプラインなどを標的にしたと明らかにした。いずれも、紅海沿岸に位置するサウジの主要石油・石油化学拠点。

サウジ側はフーシ派が発射した弾道ミサイル２発を迎撃し、一部の破片はメッカがある地域にも落下したと発表。これに対しフーシ派は聖地メッカとメディナへの攻撃を否定し、作戦は「サウジの石油施設と軍事基地を標的としている」と表明した。

一方、今月上旬にフーシ派の攻撃を受けて以来、閉鎖をしていたキング・ハリド国際空港は２４日夜、２つのターミナルについて発着を２５日から再開すると発表した。その数時間後、フーシ派の報道官は、空港を標的にした軍事作戦を続けるとして、全ての航空会社、空港職員、旅行者に対し利用を控えるよう改めて警告を発した。

item.title: Obama unloads on Trump while stumping for Democrats ahead of midterms
item.description: Barack Obama framed the Nov. 3 midterm elections vote as a "circuit breaker" to "at least rein in some of the foolishness" of Trump's presidency.
item.dc:creator: Dan Catchpole
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump has been telling voters to view the midterm elections as if he were on the ballot, and on Saturday one of his Democratic predecessors did just that. Ten days out from the elections that will determine control of the closely divided Congress, Barack Obama took to the campaign trail to accuse the Republican president of corruption, deride his strategy for Iran and skewer the gilded aesthetic he has applied to White House renovations. Obama stumped for Democratic candidates at rallies in Cleveland and Detroit, lampooning the Trump administration. Campaigning in Michigan for US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, Obama framed the November 3 vote as a "circuit breaker" to "at least rein in some of the foolishness" of Trump's presidency. "We got to flip that circuit breaker, bring some accountability to this government," Obama said. Obama, president from 2009 until Trump began his first term in 2017, remains one of the most popular figures among Democrats. They hope that bringing him into the race can fire up their supporters for a tight US Senate race in which El-Sayed faces Republican Mike Rogers, a former US representative. The former president obliged the Michigan crowd by playing to Democrats' frequently repeated criticisms of Trump and of Republicans' willingness to go along with him. "We have never seen a president excel in straight-up grifting, on your dime, like this," Obama said. "Never seen a president so intent on selling favors like this ... Now the party seems to stand for corrupt government, or inept government, or no government." The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. But in a Truth Social post on early Sunday morning, Trump called Obama a "grossly incompetent President" and labeled El-Sayed a "Muslim Brotherhood Jihadist, who hates Jews and Blacks and AMERICANS and TRUMP". A Reuters/Ipsos poll in August found that 63% of Americans think the president and his family have [USN:L6N44F13X TEXT:"inappropriately profited"] from cryptocurrency since he returned to the White House last year and that 69% believe his policy decisions are influenced by his private business dealings. Obama also ridiculed the administration's claims of victory against Iran. He argued that the war has given Iran more economic leverage because its threats to attack shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have unsettled oil exporters. "Iran now has veto power over the Strait of Hormuz, where oil goes through to get to the world," Obama said. In his social media post, Trump derided the Obama administration's approach to the Iranians, saying that he "paid off Iran with $Billions, and gave them a road to a Nuclear Weapon" with his 2015 [USN:L6N42K0ZD TEXT:"Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action"] accord with Iran. The United States withdrew from the 2015 agreement during Trump's first term. The former president also accused the Trump administration of emphasizing unimportant matters, sarcastically calling Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth someone "laser-focused on important matters like the jawline and testosterone levels of our troops" and ridiculing White House renovations as tacky. "He's got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory," Obama said.

item.title: Serbia votes in historic election as students seek to end Vucic's long grip on power
item.description: Serbian voters turned out in force on Sunday as a mass student protest movement sought to unseat longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vucic in the biggest challenge to his rule for more than a decade.
item.dc:creator: Ivana Sekularac, Edward Mcallister, Aleksandar Vasovic
item.content:encoded: Serbian voters turned out in force on Sunday as a mass student protest movement sought to unseat longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vucic in the biggest challenge to his rule for more than a decade. The [USN:L8N46618N TEXT:"snap parliamentary elections"], called by Vucic in September, come after almost two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption and creeping authoritarianism triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the city of Novi Sad in 2024. The students have since [USN:L8N4650K6 TEXT:"gained widespread support"]. Unusually long lines snaked from polling stations in cities and towns across the country. Pollsters and monitors CeSID and Ipsos put turnout at 27.3% by 11 a.m. (1000 GMT), nearly double the 15.1% at the same time in the previous election in 2023. Even Vucic waited in line for nearly two hours to vote. First indications of results are expected around two hours after polls close at 8 p.m. (1900 GMT). A student victory would be a profound political shift in the Balkan country of some 6 million people, reminiscent of the [USN:L1N40V01B TEXT:"defeat of Hungary's Viktor Orban"] in April. It could also offer a blueprint for other student movements across Europe, which have [USN:L6N464038 TEXT:"taken to the streets"] in recent weeks to protest, [USN:L2N46A01A TEXT:"in some cases violently"], against poor education standards and a lack of prospects. "It is very important for all people to come and vote if they want to change something and I think it is a time for change," said lawyer Marija Cvjeticanin at a Belgrade polling station. Vucic, who resigned from his second term as president to run again for prime minister, is a strong incumbent. Many voters thank him for pulling Serbia from economic obscurity and orchestrating a period of sustained modernisation including new highways, railways, schools and hospitals. OPINION POLLS PREDICT TIGHT RACE Vucic has pledged higher pensions and public sector salaries, and investment in state healthcare. Internationally, he has sought closer ties with China, a major investor, and remained close to Russia, Serbia's traditional ally and principal supplier of natural gas. At the same time, he still says he wants to join the European Union, Serbia's largest trading partner, but the bloc has become [USN:L6N3Z90I6 TEXT:"increasingly frustrated"] with a lack of reform. "I voted for our children, our young people...our children deserve peace and work, only Vucic can bring that," said Hatidza, a Roma woman. The students' domestic agenda aims to root out graft and improve schooling, but they have been quieter on their international ambitions. Their list of 250 largely unknown candidates includes university professors, actors and farmers, and is led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, although it is not clear who would be prime minister should they win. "I hope that today will pass in a democratic atmosphere, in peace, and that we will legitimately elect a new government in Serbia," Srdanovic said after casting his vote in Novi Sad, adding that the scenes suggested there would be a record voter turnout in the country's recent history. After casting his vote, Vucic said he would respect the result. "If we lose we will acknowledge the will of the electorate, if we win no one will take it (from us)," he said. Opinion polls ahead of the vote predicted a tight race. The head of the Election Commission, Vladimir Dimitrijevic, said voting had so far passed without incident, but monitoring bodies CeSID and CRTA pointed to incidents related to the electoral roll and secrecy of voting. STUDENT PROTESTS INCREASE PRESSURE ON VUCIC The student-led street protests sparked by the station disaster quickly became the biggest in a generation, calling for Vucic to step down. Rights groups and activists say [USN:L8N4612LD TEXT:"repression has worsened"] in the period since. "For decades the people have been waiting for this time, something to bring hope that we can live freely and by the rules of democracy," said actor Jelena Stupljanin, 48, at a Belgrade polling station. Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) have repeatedly denied accusations of repression, corruption and spying on their opponents. He says the students are funded by foreign agents in Croatia and Montenegro, a charge the students dismiss. "This has been one of the most difficult but the most emotional campaigns," Vucic told his supporters on Thursday. "We stood against those who wanted to destroy Serbia."

item.title: ゴルフ＝ＢＭＷ女子選手権、吉田が首位と4打差の2位浮上
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - 米女子ゴルフのＢＭＷ女子選手権は２４日、韓国南西部・海南のパインビーチ・リンクス（パー７２）で第３ラウンドを行い、吉田優利が２位に浮上した。

６位でスタートした吉田は５バーディー、１ボギーの４アンダー６８をマーク。通算１３アンダーの２０３に伸ばし、パク・ミンジ、チェ・ヘジン（ともに韓国）と並んだ。単独首位のユ・ヘラン（韓国）とは４打差。

畑岡奈紗と岩井明愛は通算８アンダーの１９位。吉田と同じ６位で出た岩井千怜は３オーバー７５で回り、通算６アンダーの２６位に後退した。

勝みなみは通算２アンダーの４５位。古江彩佳は通算１アンダーの５４位。原英莉花と竹田麗央は通算２オーバーの７５位となった。

item.title: フィギュア＝ＧＰ第1戦フランス大会、中井亜美が2連覇達成
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - フィギュアスケートのグランプリ（ＧＰ）シリーズ第１戦、フランス大会は２４日、アンジェで競技を行い、女子では中井亜美が合計２１９．７４で逆転優勝。同大会２連覇を果たした。

ショートプログラム（ＳＰ）３位だった中井は、フリーではトリプルアクセル（３回転半ジャンプ）を成功させて１位となった。ＳＰ首位の青木祐奈はフリーでは５位にとどまり、合計２００．６２点の４位。住吉りをんは合計１９０．７０点で６位だった。

男子ＳＰでは、山本草太が７７．０２点で８位。三浦佳生は７２．６７点で９位だった。アダム・シアオイムファ（フランス）が１０２．４６点で首位に立った。

item.title: Saudi says Riyadh airport partly reopens despite renewed Houthi threats
item.description: Saudi Arabia said its main airport resumed operations at two terminals on Sunday even as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis vowed to keep striking the facility, saying it remained a "military target".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia said its main airport resumed operations at two terminals on Sunday even as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis vowed to keep striking the facility, saying it remained a "military target". King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had halted operations on October 10 following an attack claimed by the Houthis that killed 13 people, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. Saudi Arabia intercepted another wave of missiles and drones on Sunday as fighting with the militant group continued unabated. The conflict has become an increasingly destabilising element in the US-Israeli offensive against Iran , turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in the wider war. FLIGHT TRACKING DATA SHOWS LITTLE TRAFFIC After Saudi authorities announced the partial resumption of operations at the airport, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree vowed the facility would "never be safe" and urged airlines, airport staff and travellers not to use it. Late on Saturday, the airport said Terminal 1 would be designated for domestic flights and Terminal 2 for international flights operated by national carriers starting Sunday. Despite the announcement, flight tracking data from Flightradar24 showed little traffic at the airport on Sunday. The Saudi-led coalition said earlier this month that the Houthis had carried out 20 attacks on the airport between October 1 and 11. MISSILE AND DRONE ATTACKS CONTINUE Saudi civil defense said on Sunday that shrapnel from the interception of two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis over Khamis Mushait and Ahad Rafidah injured two people and damaged residential buildings and vehicles. Civil defense authorities earlier issued emergency alerts for Riyadh and the cities of Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran on Sunday, before saying minutes later that the danger had passed. The coalition said two drones and a ballistic missile were launched towards Riyadh, and a cruise missile towards the southern city of Khamis Mushait. It later said it intercepted 10 ballistic missiles fired towards southern Saudi Arabia. The Houthis said they attacked the airport and Saudi oil facilities on Saturday. Saudi authorities did not comment directly on the Houthi statements. Saudi Arabia has stepped up its strikes against the Houthis after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month, closing in on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait – a global maritime chokepoint and shipping route for Gulf oil producers on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula to the Strait of Hormuz. The renewed fighting in Yemen has shattered a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022. Saudi Arabia intervened in Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of a coalition supporting the internationally recognised government, after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa a year earlier.

item.title: Commentary: Trump should reject Putin’s plan for a great powers summit
item.description: There’s little prospect of true negotiation on the Ukraine war until after the winter, says Marc Champion for Bloomberg Opinion.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Commentary

Commentary: Trump should reject Putin’s plan for a great powers summit

There’s little prospect of true negotiation on the Ukraine war until after the winter, says Marc Champion for Bloomberg Opinion.

Visitors stand in front of an artwork depicting US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping at an exhibition, which is called "Yalta 2.0" and opened to make a reference to the 1945 Yalta Conference, at an art gallery in Livadia park in Yalta, Crimea, Feb 8, 2025. REUTERS/Alexey Pavlishak

Marc Champion

FAST

LONDON: The mere prospect of Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump meeting for a great-powers summit while at the Asia Pacific Economic Community’s annual gathering next month is causing concern among America’s traditional allies, not to mention Ukraine. Rightly so. One reason for caution is the very fact that Putin has been pressing for this for some time, most recently in his Oct 9 phone call with the US president. The Kremlin says preparations are underway, but Trump should ask why it is that Moscow is so interested before he commits to attending. One attraction is that the plan would exclude Ukraine and Europe, the two objects of Russian aggression and therefore the ones most likely to get in the way of the wider deal Putin is looking for. Indeed, when US Special Envoy for Peace Missions Steve Witkoff this week delivered an updated ceasefire proposal he worked out with Ukrainian and Europeans leaders in Oslo, the response from Kremlin point-man Yuri Ushakov was dismissive. It lacked substance, he said.

The charade around peace efforts will continue for a while yet; Ushakov said the Russians might be interested in resuming lower-level talks next month, before the possible three-way summit at APEC’s Nov 18 to 19 meeting in Southern China. But there’s little prospect of a true negotiation until after the winter. Putin believes he has a big enough advantage in the long-range air war that he will emerge next spring with a rump Ukraine that has either capitulated or lies in ruins. He would count either as a win.

WHAT TRUMP AND PUTIN CAN GAIN Trump doesn’t appear to care about this, as he’s more interested in the potential commercial benefits of a US-Russia reset. So this week he ignored all evidence of daily Russian attacks on civilian targets to say that Russia was “fine” on Ukraine and “hasn’t been doing much”. Witkoff, meeting Putin on Wednesday (Oct 21), even praised Russia’s president as “a humanitarian”. Two days earlier, one of Putin’s Shahed-style loitering munitions – which circle until locked onto something to strike – had killed six people in a park in Ukraine’s Kharkiv region. The victims included a one-year-old girl in a stroller, together with her mother and two more children; 14 others, including other children, were wounded. Trump no doubt bets he can blame the war’s continuation on Europe and Zelenskyy, and that news of Russian oil tankers steaming toward the US with diesel (to lower prices at the pump) will help him politically ahead of the midterms on Nov 3. Sadly, some American voters may agree, while the gravitas and razzmatazz that a great-powers summit brings could help, too.  For Putin, the stakes are higher. From the day his armies invaded in 2022, he has made clear that his goal is not just to seize territory, but to change the entire security architecture of Europe in a way that allows Russia to restore influence across the continent and reestablish itself as a great power. A three-way meeting in China would plant a decisive flag in that quest and is made yet more attractive by the fact that Xi is a close ally. It would be two against one, on Xi’s home turf. I would happily support giving Putin that win if it would unlock the door to compromise on Ukraine and other points of global tension. But that isn’t how it would work. Putin does not want recognition of Russia as a great power just for reasons of status. He seeks the right to do what great powers do: establish dominance over the nations around them.

Related:

Commentary: This is an era of Davids, not Goliaths

Commentary: Russia’s new jet‑powered drones mark latest evolution in air war above Ukraine

A SECOND YALTA CONFERENCE Hence the excitement in Russia’s state-controlled media over the possibility that Shenzhen could serve as a second Yalta conference. At the first, in 1945, Winston Churchill, Franklin D Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin not only created a framework for the United Nations but also agreed to enable the self-determination – via free democratic elections – of the countries they occupied. Stalin, of course, reneged, continuing the de-facto Soviet occupation of what later would become the Warsaw Pact. To his credit, Trump seems to be pushing discussion of the potential China summit’s agenda toward nuclear arms control, not Ukraine or spheres of influence. This is an important area for diplomacy. It’s also one in which US and Russian interests coincide against China’s. Xi is building his country’s nuclear arsenal quickly, but it remains far from parity, which would likely make any arms-control deal that would suit Moscow and Washington unattractive to Beijing. How would it then catch up? That’s one reason the meeting might not happen, which might be for the best given the checkered record that great-power summits enjoy. They tend to depend heavily on both the balance of power on the day and the relative personal strengths and weaknesses of the leaders involved. Munich, in 1938, needs no further comment. Yalta was shaped by the fact that three wartime allies at the table still had millions of troops on the ground, while Roosevelt was sick with heart disease and a brain tumour (he died soon afterward) and together with Churchill overly trusting of Stalin, who played them. A divided Europe and the Cold War followed. John F Kennedy’s 1961 summit with Nikita Khrushchev was a diplomatic car crash that would have been better skipped. Khrushchev came away thinking Kennedy weak, unprepared and undisciplined. The Berlin airlift and Cuban missile crisis followed, as the Soviet leader tried to press an advantage he thought he had.

Related:

Commentary: Trump’s Russian diesel U-turn comes at bad time for Ukraine

Commentary: America is risking its biggest asset

ASSESSING TRUMP’S PROSPECTS So how to assess Trump’s prospects in Shenzhen, should the summit materialise? The first thing to say is that the US president has a track record in high-profile summitry that is not encouraging. He has repeatedly given leverage away for nothing in his dealings with Putin, proving himself far too trusting of a career intelligence handler. His red carpet meetings with the Russian leader in Anchorage last year, and with North Korea’s Kim Jong Un in 2018, both suffered from poor preparation akin to Kennedy’s. Trump is notorious for not engaging with detail and there would be just weeks for sherpas to prepare. Second, the wider circumstances would not be propitious for any American leader. The US is engaged in a draining war that has no obvious path to success in Iran, a country supported by both China and Russia. This gives them leverage in any negotiation, whereas Trump already gave up much of his in Ukraine by withdrawing most US support. America’s strong alliances in Europe and Asia – formerly a major advantage over both Beijing and Moscow – are weakening, undermined primarily by US actions. Those ties would be further damaged by any agreement made over their heads in China, especially if it were to trade their geopolitical loss for US commercial gain, as Trump is wont to do. Even if there were no attempt at a second Yalta and a three-way meeting took place in Shenzhen for purely symbolic value, it could still have costs in the form of distraction. For amid all the noise, the world would be led to believe something was being done to end Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and its potential for escalation in Europe, when it wasn’t. That works only for Putin.

Source: Bloomberg/el
